attributes.provenance: src/game/game/pmotion.c::get_player_pos, worktree GDL-Claude-PmotionDr3, commit b50211dc1. The function arrived carrying a recorded residual_class of REGISTER_ONLY, justified in attempt.get-player-pos-view-pointer-identity.20260831.v1 by insns 506/506 with an IDENTICAL opcode multiset (0t) and a matching frame and save-set - a characterisation reached over several sessions and never doubted. A single scripted pass over fndiff --clean, normalising each paired diff line by replacing every register token with a placeholder and comparing the results, flagged 16 of the differing words as NOT explainable by any renaming. Six of them were `lfs f0,100(rBase)` in the target against `lfs f0,84(rBase)` in ours, at two sites. Offsets 0x54 and 0x64 are col_pos and effectpos, both already present and GC-verified in include/game/player.h: the reconstruction was reading the wrong field of Player in get_player_pos's partner-spawn probe. Correcting it required no header change and no new name, moved the six words out of structural mismatch and into the function's register permutation, and lifted fuzzy 97.7688% -> 97.7806%.

subject: function:get_player_pos
value: AN IDENTICAL OPCODE MULTISET DOES NOT ESTABLISH A REGISTER_ONLY RESIDUAL. AGENTS.md reads the `opcode multiset:` line as the classifier - IDENTICAL means pure reorder, DIFFERS means structure is hiding - and that reading is correct as far as it goes, but it has a blind spot that has now cost this project multiple sessions of misdirected probing. The multiset is computed over OPCODES. It therefore cannot see a difference in a memory operand's DISPLACEMENT: `lfs f0,84(r20)` and `lfs f0,100(r19)` are both `lfs` and contribute identically. A wrong struct field, a wrong array index, and a wrong stack slot are all invisible to it, and all three also preserve the instruction COUNT, so insn-exactness corroborates the wrong conclusion rather than catching it. `real` is no help either: the word differed before the fix and still differs after it (only its REASON changes from structural to renaming), so the count is flat and the edit reads NEUTRAL - the same blindness claim.law.value-identity-split-completes-a-broken-recolor-bijection.20260831.v1 documents for its own transformation. Three metrics agreeing on REGISTER_ONLY can thus all be wrong together. THE TEST, which is cheap, mechanical, and should be run ONCE on every function before any register or schedule theory is funded: take fndiff --clean, pair the - and + lines within each equal-length hunk, normalise both by substituting a placeholder for every register token, and compare. Words that still differ after normalisation are NOT renaming residual and are structural by construction - displacements, immediates, relocation targets, branch shapes. On get_player_pos this took one script and one build and found a genuine field-selection bug in a function three prior sessions had already classified as pure colouring. COROLLARY, and the reason to run the same normalisation over the whole function rather than only the flagged hunk: the identical test applied to stack displacements gave the frame residual for free - a full census of every (r1) reference on both sides showed all named locals and the save area agreeing exactly and isolated the entire frame delta to the two fabs-idiom compiler temps. SECOND COROLLARY, on how the mischaracterisation arose in the first place: when the same normalisation is used to TALLY a candidate permutation, tally it by fitting a single sigma and then testing the remainder, never by taking a majority target per register. The per-register majority/minority tally reported get_player_pos as 'a permutation failing bijection at five split sources'; fitting one sigma showed a clean 12-cycle on GPRs plus a 3-cycle on FPRs with 111 of 125 words conforming and only 14 deviating. The two readings differ in what they tell the next agent to do, and only the second one is actionable.
